acceptance_checks: All five workflows declare a concurrency block with cancel-in-progress: true and a group expression that distinguishes pull requests from one another.
_check_bucket maps cancelled, skipped and stale to the non-terminal bucket, and still maps failure and an unrecognised value to fail.
decide_task_action does not dispatch a repair for a PR whose only non-green required check is cancelled — asserted through the decision function, not by inspection.
A labeled event carrying guardian:approved starts the CCA job.
A labeled event carrying any mergegate:* mode label starts the CCA job.
A labeled event carrying an unrelated label does not start the CCA job.
The CCA judge step does not execute while a required check other than CCA's own is still pending on the current head, and the wait is bounded with a clear timeout message.
CCA-06 remains blocking and docs/agents/checklists.md is unchanged.
No step that posts a review, comment or label carries if: always(); the CCA Review Bridge in particular does not.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests, scripts/test_shiki_workflow_lint.sh, scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh and validate_shiki all pass.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: Moving CCA to a workflow_run trigger
Removing labeled from the CCA trigger, or excluding guardian:approved or any mergegate:* label from the filter
Changing CCA-06's severity or any entry in docs/agents/checklists.md
Changing the verdict schema, any verdict value, or what the judge evaluates
Adding if: always() to any step that posts a review, comment or label
Changing the repair attempt limit or any MergeGate rule
Deleting or disabling the Shiki Claude Review workflow
Touching any file outside the declared locks

findings.detail: shiki-orchestrator.yml triggers only on issue_comment and workflow_dispatch, so github.event.pull_request.number is always empty and the concurrency group becomes ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }} (refs/heads/main for every issue_comment). With cancel-in-progress: true, an unrelated /shiki comment on a different issue/PR can cancel another conversation's in-flight run, contradicting the scope's 'never touches a different one'. Real harm is low because the issue_comment path (shiki-run) is a read-only --dry-run and the mutating commit-evidence job runs only on workflow_dispatch execute-github (per-ref, rarely concurrent). Recommend keying this workflow on github.event.issue.number || github.ref.
findings.title: Orchestrator concurrency key never resolves per-conversation (collapses to github.ref)

findings.detail: A job skipped by the new label if: reports its check run as skipped, which _check_bucket now maps to pending. If a human adds a non-verdict label (e.g. documentation) to an already-green PR, the CCA/MergeGate check can be shadowed by a skipped run and the loop shifts to wait_checks with nothing scheduled to re-run CCA. In normal loop operation the loop re-triggers CCA via guardian:approved/mergegate labels, so this only bites on out-of-band labels; it is an accepted tradeoff of the (c)+(b) design but worth noting.
findings.title: Skipped label-filtered check maps to pending, can stall the loop on an out-of-band label

scope:
Remove three measured causes of redundant Completion Check Agent runs, and the one coupling that would make the first of them harmful.

(a) CONCURRENCY. Add a `concurrency:` block with `cancel-in-progress: true` to all five workflows: shiki-cca-completion.yml, shiki-mergegate.yml, shiki-validate.yml, shiki-claude-review.yml, shiki-orchestrator.yml. Key the group per workflow and per pull request so that a newer event supersedes an older run on the SAME pull request and never touches a different one — `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}` is the intended shape. Measured today: `grep -c '^concurrency:'` is 0 in all five; shiki runs 200 CCA runs over 154 distinct head SHAs (27 pairs within 180s on the same SHA) and CubeShare 200 over 135 (46 such pairs, five SHAs at 4 runs).

(b) THE COUPLING — SAME COMMIT AS (a), NOT A SEPARATE ONE. `scripts/shiki_loop.py:580` `_check_bucket` returns "fail" for anything outside {pass, success} and {pending, queued, in_progress}. A `cancelled` conclusion therefore reads as a FAILED required check, and the loop dispatches a repair against a run that was merely superseded. Widen the non-terminal bucket to also cover `cancelled`, `skipped` and `stale`. Landing (a) without (b) makes the loop strictly worse than it is today: it converts every cancellation into a wasted repair attempt.

(c) LABEL FILTERING. Both shiki-cca-completion.yml and shiki-mergegate.yml trigger on `labeled` and `unlabeled`, so every label costs a full run. Measured on shiki PR #323 head b635454c: the timeline shows `07:35:29 labeled mergegate:contract` and `07:37:25 labeled guardian:approved`, and CCA ran at 07:35, 07:35 and 07:37. GitHub cannot filter by label name in `on:`, so add a JOB-LEVEL `if:` that proceeds only when the event is not a label event, or when the label is one that can change the verdict. `guardian:approved` and every `mergegate:*` mode label MUST remain in that set — CCA-08 reads the Guardian approval source, and removing it would pin the verdict at needs_guardian forever. A skipped job costs no runner minutes.

(d) SETTLED-CHECK GATE. The `Prepare CCA context` step reads check state once, at the top of its own run: `gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --json ...,statusCheckRollup > .shiki/gha/pr.json`. Because CCA triggers on the same `pull_request` event as CI, Validate and MergeGate, those checks are still pending, and CCA-06 ('Required checks pass on current head SHA.', blocking, checklists.md:183) cannot pass. Before the judge is invoked, wait until the required checks other than CCA's own have reached a terminal conclusion on the current head, with a bounded timeout and a clear message when the timeout is hit. Do NOT relax CCA-06 — this is an ordering fix, not a judgement fix. Do NOT move the workflow to a `workflow_run` trigger; that was considered and rejected on trust-boundary grounds.

MUST NOT: add `if: always()` to any step that posts a review, comment or label — the `CCA Review Bridge` step submits `--arg event "APPROVE"` and an always-run bridge would mint an approval on a refused verdict. Do not change docs/agents/checklists.md, the verdict schema, any verdict value, the repair attempt limit, any MergeGate rule, or scripts/mergegate_check.py. Do not delete or disable the Shiki Claude Review workflow.

TESTS. `tests/test_cca_rerun_economy.py` (new): all five workflows parse and each declares `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true` and a group expression that includes the pull request number; the CCA and MergeGate jobs' `if:` admits `guardian:approved` and each `mergegate:*` mode label and rejects an unrelated label such as `documentation`; no step whose `run:` or `uses:` posts a review, comment or label carries `if: always()`. `tests/test_loop_engine.py`: `_check_bucket` maps `cancelled`, `skipped` and `stale` to the non-terminal bucket while `failure` and an unknown value still map to fail, and `decide_task_action` does not dispatch a repair for a PR whose only non-green required check is cancelled. `tests/test_workflow_invocation.py` reconstructs mergegate_check.py's argv from the workflow `run:` steps and raises KeyError without a matching `_FLAG_VALUES` entry — keep it green; if a new `run:` step changes what it parses, update it without weakening any existing assertion.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: a single head SHA accumulates two to four full Claude CCA runs, each several minutes, and the first run on any new head cannot return `complete` no matter what the implementation does, so a human re-runs it by hand.
  Measured 2026-08-17: shiki 200 runs / 154 SHAs = 1.30x (27 near-simultaneous same-SHA pairs); CubeShare 200 / 135 = 1.48x (46 pairs, worst SHA 4 runs); CubeShare's CCA workflow consumed 523 minutes over 74 runs on 2026-08-10 alone.
  Root causes: no `concurrency:` in any of the five workflows; `labeled`/`unlabeled` in the CCA and MergeGate trigger types with no label filter; and a CCA job that reads `statusCheckRollup` at the top of a run that starts concurrently with the very checks CCA-06 requires to be green.
  Trap that makes a partial fix harmful: `shiki_loop.py:580` buckets `cancelled` as `fail`, so cancellation without the bucket widening converts each superseded run into a dispatched repair.
  Reproducible when: a second push or label on a pull request cancels the in-flight run instead of adding one; a cancelled check leaves the loop's decision unchanged; an unrelated label starts nothing; and the judge does not start while the checks it reads are pending.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target . && bash scripts/test_shiki_workflow_lint.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh
title: Cancel superseded runs, gate CCA on settled checks, and stop reading a cancelled check as a failure
